records.title: Efficient Detection of Intermittent Job Failures Using Few-Shot Learning
records.venue: IEEE International Conference on Software Maintenance (ICSM)
records.authors: Henri Aïdasso; Francis Bordeleau; Ali Tizghadam
records.abstract: One of the main challenges developers face in the use of continuous integration (CI) and deployment pipelines is the occurrence of intermittent job failures, which result from unexpected non-deterministic issues (e.g., flaky tests or infrastructure problems) rather than regular code-related errors such as bugs. Prior studies developed machine learning (ML) models trained on large datasets of job logs to classify job failures as either intermittent or regular. As an alternative to costly manual labeling of large datasets, the state-of-the-art (SOTA) approach leveraged a heuristic based on non-deterministic job reruns. However, this method mislabels intermittent job failures as regular in contexts where rerunning suspicious job failures is not an explicit policy, and therefore limits the SOTA's performance in practice. In fact, our manual analysis of 2,125 job failures from 5 industrial and 1 open-source projects reveals that, on average, 32 % of intermittent job failures are mislabeled as regular. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel approach to intermittent job failure detection using fewshot learning (FSL). Specifically, we fine-tune a small language model using a few number of manually labeled log examples to generate rich embeddings, which are then used to train an ML classification head. Our FSL-based approach achieves 70 - 88% F1-score with only 12 shots in all projects, outperforming the SOTA, which proved ineffective (34-52% F1-score) in 4 projects. Overall, this study underlines the importance of data quality over quantity and provides a more efficient and practical framework for the detection of intermittent job failures in organizations.

records.title: SELF-HEALING WEB AUTOMATION: AN EMPIRICAL COMPARISON OF TRADITIONAL SELENIUM FRAMEWORKS AND HEALENIUM STACK
records.venue: International Journal of Apllied Mathematics
records.authors: Savi Grover
records.abstract: Web user interfaces and mobile applications change rapidly and even minor modifications in the element address or Document Object Model (DOM) can invalidate test locators, causing brittle, flaky test suites and unstable CI/CD pipelines. Self-healing automation frameworks aim to reduce this fragility by automatically recovering from locator breakage at runtime. This paper presents a practical approach for understanding self-healing web automation and its various methodology like – Healenium and Selenide. We describe how they work, provide code-level details and propose an experimental setup that compares traditional Selenium tests with healing tests against a self-healing stack on many dimensions: locator-related flakiness, maintenance effort, and test execution time. Experimentation results indicate that self-healing can reduce locator-related failures by 40–60% and maintenance effort by 30–50%, at the cost of minor execution overhead. We discuss threats to validity, limitations, and how this pattern generalizes with mobile and API automation.

records.title: Regression test prioritization for modern software
records.venue: Illinois Digital Environment for Access to Learning and Scholarship (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign)
records.authors: Runxiang Cheng
records.abstract: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in software development for increasing code quality. CI runs regression test suite on each code change to help software developers find faults in the change. As codebase size and code change frequency have grown rapidly in modern software development, regression test suite runtime has also increased, thereby preventing timely debugging feedback to developers. Regression Test Prioritization (RTP) aims to expose faults in code change sooner by reordering tests in the test suite, so that the ones likely to fail are run earlier. Despite that RTP has been extensively studied for nearly three decades, research results of RTP are rarely put into practice. To facilitate the adoption of RTP for modern software systems, RTP must be demonstrated effective in speeding up regression fault detection in relevant and practical testing settings. Moreover, robust and efficient RTP tooling must be available for practitioners to easily apply RTP research results in popular software ecosystems. This dissertation takes a step forward in addressing these challenges via three lines of work. First, this dissertation examines key research findings from prior RTP studies on a newly-proposed dataset of long-running test suites with real test failures and up-to-date CI practices. Through extensive evaluation, this dissertation identifies the most effective and efficient RTP techniques under the impact of realistic CI issues such as flaky test failures. Second, this dissertation applies traditional RTP techniques for configuration testing, an emerging but critical testing scenario; it further proposes novel and effective RTP techniques for configuration testing. This dissertation assesses various factors that influence the effectiveness of RTP in speeding up misconfiguration detection, and provides detailed analyses and guidelines in applying RTP to configuration tests. Third, this dissertation presents pytest-ranking, a readily-usable open-source RTP tool for Python and its most popular testing framework Pytest. This dissertation realistically evaluates the efficacy of pytest-ranking, demonstrating that pytest-ranking is well integrated with Python/Pytest ecosystems, can be conveniently deployed into CI, has low overhead, and can detect faults substantially faster than baselines.

records.title: Continuous Testing in Agile and DevOps Environments
records.venue: Journal of Contemporary Science and Technology Management
records.authors: Toussida Fatah Tanguy Minoungou; Aisha I. Abdulwahab; Harouna Wendpanga Yann Christian Sankara; Samuel Fadero; Olumide Kumuyi
records.abstract: Background: Continuous testing promises that every change to a software system is evaluated automatically and quickly enough for the result to shape the next decision. Many agile and DevOps teams nonetheless run large automated suites whose verdicts they no longer trust, because flaky tests, queued pipelines, and drifting environments turn a failing build into noise. Aim: The review asks how test portfolio shape, test stability, pipeline feedback latency, and environment parity jointly determine whether continuous testing yields decision-grade evidence, and how that evidence relates to delivery outcomes such as the DORA metrics. Method: A critical integrative review of software testing, continuous integration, traceability, and empirical software engineering literature published up to 2025 was interpreted through signal detection theory and queueing-based feedback control. Results: Execution speed and suite size are weak proxies for assurance. The positive predictive value of a failing build collapses as small per-test flake rates compound across large suites, and latency that outlasts the developer's working context converts feedback into rework. Contribution: The article proposes the Continuous Testing Signal Integrity (CTSI) framework, which separates detection capability, false-alarm burden, feedback latency, environment fidelity, and production evidence, and states six falsifiable propositions with a stepped-wedge validation design. Conclusion: Continuous testing should be governed as a measurement instrument whose reliability is itself monitored; the propositions are untested and are offered for prospective evaluation.

records.title: AI - Based Root Cause Analysis of Test Failures Using Allure Reports
records.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
records.authors: Alex Thomas Thomas
records.abstract: With increasingly complex and larger systems, automated testing is nowadays an embedded element of modern development prac-tices. However, root cause analysis (RCA) of test failures remains a time - consuming, knowledge - intensive, and error - prone ac-tivity that typically requires considerable domain expertise. This paper explores the use of an AI - powered RCA on test failure data extracted from Allure reports a standard test framework to generate rich, structured test outcomes. The approach utilizes machine learning methods, natural language understanding, and causality to enable automated diagnosis and classification of failures through the analysis of logs, error messages, and execution traces. It not only accelerates fault localization but also improves the accuracy and uniformity of diagnosis. The review synthesizes current research trends and technology enabling intelligent RCA, re-views current frameworks and tools, and documents the incorporation of AI models into CI/CD pipelines. The paper also addresses significant issues such as interpretability of the model, data quality, and managing flaky tests. By bridging the gap between test result visualization and automated diagnosis, AI - based RCA with Allure presents a smart and scalable solution for improving software reliability and development efficiency.

records.abstract: Modern software development and CI/CD principles place high expectations on quality assurance. especially in mobile application testing, the wide variety of devices and the need to test on real physical devices create challenges for the stability of the testing infrastructure. This thesis investigates and implements the modernization of the target company's mobile testing environment. The company's previous device farm, based on VHClient and USB-over-IP technology, has proven unstable, causing random test failures ("flaky tests") and resource locking, which hinders daily development work and nightly regression runs. The objective of this work is to solve these stability and maintenance problems by designing and implementing a new Appium based Appium Device Farm which is being introduced alongside the existing system. The research method used was Design Science Research Methodology (DSRM). A distributed server architecture was set up in the work, consisting of a centralized Hub and Nodes connected to it. Additionally, the new system is integrated programmatically to enable device management and test execution. The result of the work was a functional device farm environment that meets the technical and qualitative requirements set for it. The new solution addresses the root causes of in-stability by eliminating the USB-over-IP connection used in device relay, thereby creating a more robust foundation for testing. The work demonstrates that transitioning to Appium based infrastructure is a technically viable solution for mitigating stability issues, although full integration into production CI/CD pipelines remains a topic for future development.

records.title: Doc2Test: An Industrial Multi-agent Framework for Document-Driven End-to-End Selenium Test Generation
records.venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automated Software Engineering (ASE)
records.authors: Andrea Lops; Antonio Ferrara; Fedelucio Narducci; Azzurra Ragone; Michelantonio Trizio
records.abstract: End-to-end (E2E) testing is a persistent industrial bottleneck: Selenium, a widely used open-source framework for automating web browsers via scripted interactions that emulate user behaviour, relies on brittle scripts, while off-the-shelf Large Language Models (LLMs) hallucinate selectors and saturate the context window when asked to synthesise complete user journeys over production DOMs. We present Doc2Test, a Multi-Agent System (MAS) deployed inside Wideverse (a software engineering and digital transformation ICT company) that translates unstructured requirement documents into executable Selenium suites through three specialised phases: requirements analysis, dynamic DOM/visual context perception, and adaptive code generation with a self-healing loop. Across 90 independent runs on a production Angular cruise-booking platform (∼145k LoC, under NDA), four open-sourced internal Wideverse applications, and one independently-developed external application (RealWorld), Doc2Test achieves a 94.4% generation success rate (95% CI: [87.5%, 98.2%]), detects 98.9% of 180 injected UI regressions, and reduces token usage by 86% against a zero-shot single-prompt baseline. Over three months of nightly Jenkins operation, it reduced maintenance effort by ∼2.6 person-days / sprint and the flaky-test rate from 11.4% to 4.6%. We further report cost breakdowns and deployment lessons from integrating Doc2Test into our industrial partner’s CI/CD pipeline.

records.title: Test Automation Frameworks for Microservices-Based Applications
records.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Computer Science and Engineering
records.authors: Arpit Jain
records.abstract: Microservices architectures accelerate delivery but multiply the surface area that must be validated—APIs, asynchronous events, idempotent workflows, distributed data, and resilience under partial failure. Conventional UI-heavy or single-service test suites struggle with flakiness, long cycle times, and blind spots where inter-service contracts drift. This manuscript proposes a unified, code-centric test automation framework tailored to microservices. The framework layers fast unit and component tests, consumer-driven contract (CDC) tests for synchronous and evented interfaces, containerized integration tests with ephemeral environments, and lightweight end-to-end, performance, security, and chaos checks. It standardizes on executable specifications, test data versioning, service virtualization, and observability-driven assertions (logs, metrics, and traces) wired into CI/CD. We evaluate the framework in a simulated e-commerce domain (six services, HTTP + Kafka) across 12 sprints, comparing it with (a) a baseline manual + UI/E2E approach and (b) a traditional API-automation stack. The proposed framework improved pre-production defect detection by 36.8%, cut CI test duration by 63.0%, reduced flaky tests by 74.4%, and lowered escaped defects per release by 78.6%—while enabling 92% contract coverage. Results suggest that embracing CDC, containerized integration, and observability-backed assertions in a layered pyramid materially improves feedback speed and reliability without over-investing in brittle end-to-end suites. We conclude with guidance for adoption, limits, and opportunities for future enhancement.

records.title: Autonomous AI and Agentic Testing Agents: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Self-Directed Software Quality Assurance
records.venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence Machine Learning and Data Science
records.authors: urvish Gajjar
records.abstract: Software testing has historically depended on scripted automation and human-crafted test oracles, both of which struggle to keep pace with continuously evolving user interfaces, microservice topologies and release cadences.This paper presents an architecture and workflow for Autonomous AI and Agentic Testing Agents, a class of systems in which large language model (LLM)-driven agents perceive an application under test, reason about test intent, generate and execute test cases, self-heal broken locators, triage defects and continuously learn from historical outcomes with minimal human supervision.We describe a layered, multi-agent architecture composed of perception, reasoning, execution, tool-integration and reporting layers and we present an end-to-end workflow that closes the loop between test generation, execution, root-cause analysis and memory-based learning.We further discuss an illustrative implementation using Python-and JavaScript-based agents integrated with common test frameworks and CI/CD pipelines, present representative code artifacts and report qualitative observations on test-authoring effort, self-healing effectiveness and flaky-test reduction drawn from a pilot deployment.The paper concludes with a discussion of open challenges -non-determinism oracle construction, explainability and trust -together with directions for future research on agentic quality assurance.

records.title: Collaborative Intelligence in DevSecOps: A Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous Vulnerability Detection and Remediation
records.venue: ABUAD Journal of Engineering Research and Development (AJERD)
records.authors: Eyimofe Okikiola Orimolade; Aliyu Suleiman Muhammad
records.abstract: The adoption of Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) practices has accelerated software delivery but has also introduced substantial security challenges. Conventional DevSecOps approaches rely on isolated security scanning tools with high false-positive rates, and identified vulnerabilities are typically fixed manually, which delays deployments. This research aims to design and evaluate an agentic AI-powered DevSecOps framework that uses a multi-agent system to automate security tasks in the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC). The framework deploys eight specialized artificial intelligence agents, including Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), Software Composition Analysis (SCA) and remediation agents, coordinated through an event-driven message bus built with the Google Agent Development Kit (ADK) and the Gemini Large Language Model (LLM). On 228 labelled code units from WebGoat, DVWA and OWASP Juice Shop, the framework's LLM-assisted SAST agent achieved a macro-average Defect Detection Rate (DDR) of 90.36% (pooled 91.38%), compared with 27.13% for the Semgrep scanner alone (exact McNemar test, p < 0.001), at the cost of a higher false-positive rate (46.30% against 9.26%). Flaky-test classification reached an F1 score of 1.0 in a controlled simulation. Across 90 remediation cases, the Mean Time to Remediate (MTTR) from vulnerability analysis to pull-request preparation was 7.19 seconds, compared with typical manual remediation times of 2 to 4 hours. These results suggest that distributing tasks among specialized AI agents can mitigate the context-window limitations of single-agent LLM assistants. We conclude that multi-agent AI systems are a promising approach to addressing the limitations of existing security tools and single-agent assistants, provided that their false positives are controlled. This research contributes to software engineering practice and knowledge by providing an autonomous detection and remediation framework that reduces the trade-off between deployment speed and software security, and by identifying the further validation required before production use.

records.title: How to Fix Automation Flakiness: Root Causes and Enterprise-Level Solutions
records.venue: Journal of Engineering Research and Sciences
records.authors: Sujeet Kumar Tiwari
records.abstract: Flakiness in automation is one of the most intractable barriers to dependable enterprise CI/CD, in which organizations can run more than 50M tests daily, and a 5-10% flaky rate may spoil thousands of builds. The paper brings together empirical research and industrial case studies on UI, API, mobile, and data pipelines to describe the prevalent flakiness root causes, such as asynchronous UI, discontinuous DOM, unsteady test data, environment latency spikes, concurrency defects, and the absence of synchronization. It advances a multi-level stability design which incorporates deterministic locator strategies, clever wait handling, resilient API contracts, controlled test-data administration, and reliability designs of cloud-based environment patterns. The method is supported with the help of AI-supported analytics, where execution telemetry, the flakiness probability score, and heatmaps would be utilized to identify unstable tests early and devote effort to remediation. Large-scale settings reported case studies indicate a 5-10% to less than 1% drop in the rate of flaky tests, infrastructure savings of up to 2 times, and savings in diagnostic effort of up to 30-50%. The paper ends with providing explicit future directions, such as achieving a >95% accuracy on automated flakiness location, benchmark and KPI standardization, and stability engineering and integration with wider practices of reliability and governance. These guidelines will help ensure that test stability is an SRE first-class objective.

records.title: AI-Driven Test Automation in Distributed Microservices Architecture
records.venue: International Journal of Engineering Science and Information Technology
records.authors: Supratim Dutta
records.abstract: Distributed microservices architectures have shifted a substantial share of software quality effort from code development toward validating interactions among independently deployed services. As continuous integration pipelines expand to tens of thousands of test cases, traditional automation faces increasing execution costs, flaky tests, and brittle locators that require extensive engineering maintenance. This paper examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques can restructure software testing across distributed microservices environments. The study maps six classes of AI techniques to the testing phases they most effectively support and develops a reference pipeline that integrates AI-assisted test generation, test selection, failure analysis, test-data management, and self-healing automation. Comparative measurements are synthesized from production engineering data and peer-reviewed empirical studies to assess changes in execution efficiency, defect detection, and automation stability. The results indicate that AI-driven testing reduces the mean test execution time per commit by 74% and the escaped-defect rate by 63% relative to traditional testing baselines. Self-healing locator strategies achieve 95–98% stability when user-interface structure changes, reducing failures caused by locator degradation. The analysis further indicates that sustained performance depends on human-AI collaboration, particularly for validating generated tests, interpreting ambiguous failures, and governing test priorities. Test-data engineering emerges as the principal constraint limiting further improvements because AI-based generation and execution remain dependent on representative, valid, and sufficiently diverse data. The findings demonstrate that AI-driven test automation can be implemented as a measurable engineering practice with identifiable performance benefits rather than treated solely as an emerging technological concept. The proposed framework provides a structured basis for integrating AI techniques into continuous testing workflows while retaining human oversight for quality assurance and decision-making

records.title: A Comparative Study of Intelligent Synthetic Test Generation in Distributed Software Architectures for Improving Cross-Layer Validation Efficiency
records.venue: American Journal of Technology
records.authors: Naveen Prakash
records.abstract: Aim: This study aims to introduce search-based intelligent test generation for synthetic testing as a means of enabling optimal cross-layer testing in distributed software architectures comprising front-end interfaces, API gateways, microservices, databases, and cloud-based runtime services. It addresses the limitation of legacy quality assurance automation, which remains layer-isolated and rule-based, and is therefore unable to effectively detect inter-service faults, asynchronous failures, or unreliable execution behaviors in complex workflows. Methods: The research adopts a comparative mixed-methods approach, analyzing an AI-based framework that incorporates behavioral trace modeling, dependency graph generation, historical defect learning, and synthetic scenario generation. The evaluation was conducted across three types of enterprise applications, involving 30 autonomous test runs and 12 expert interviews. Results: The findings demonstrate substantial improvements in testing performance, with cross-layer validation coverage increasing to 84% and 62%, defects detected rising to 87% and 68%, and flaky tests reduced to 7% and 18%. Additionally, failure reproducibility improved by 19%, while scenario generation expanded by a factor of 2.7, increasing from 45 to 120 scenarios. Conclusion: The study concludes that synthetic test generation represents a realistic, scalable, and statistically informed approach that significantly enhances validation under realistic operating conditions, thereby providing a more reliable baseline for release confidence and operational decision-making. Recommendation: The study recommends further research focusing on reinforcement learning, explainability, increased autonomy through CI/CD integration, and the development of cross-domain benchmarks to advance the effectiveness and applicability of intelligent testing frameworks.

records.title: PROSPECTS OF USING AI FOR AUTOMATED SOFTWARE TESTING
records.venue: Technologies and Engineering
records.authors: Artem ANTONENKO; Oleksandr Golubenko; A. O. Onysko; Serhii Chechyk; С. О. Востріков
records.abstract: Purpose. The research method is to analyze the prospects for using artificial intelligence to overcome key limitations of traditional automated software testing, in particular, test fragility, low adaptability, large volumes of test scenarios and the inconsistency of testing speed with the pace of modern development, as well as to justify the transition to intelligent, self-learning quality assurance systems. Methodology. The work uses the method of systematic review and synthesis of modern scientific literature and publications of leading technology companies, a comparative analysis of traditional and AI-oriented approaches to testing, general practical use of examples using large language models, reinforcement learning, graph neural networks and self-healing technologies, as well as illustrative modeling of the benefits of AI through schematic diagrams and examples. Findings. The study identified six main problems of classical testing and demonstrated that the integration of AI allows you to automatically generate test scripts (including from natural language), predict defects, implement self-healing mechanisms, optimize test priority in CI/CD, detect flaky tests, and significantly increase code coverage and process stability while simultaneously reducing support costs autotests. Originality. The novelty lies in the systematic synthesis and updating of trends in the use of large language models for generating tests based on natural language, graph neural networks for dependency analysis, as well as reinforcement learning methods for adaptive navigation in interfaces, which simultaneously contribute to the formation of the concept of proactive, intelligent, and context-oriented software testing provision. Practical value. The results of the work have direct practical value for QA teams and DevOps processes: the proposed AI approaches allow you to reduce time and resources for supporting automated tests, accelerate CI/CD cycles, increase the reliability of releases, optimize the focus of testing on risky areas of the code, and ensure the availability of processes even for a team with limited technical resources.

records.title: Automação de Testes em Plataformas Móveis e Web: Otimização de Processos sob Metodologias Ágeis em Contexto Industrial
records.venue: Instituto Politécnico de Leiria
records.authors: Bernardo Paulo Melo
records.abstract: O presente relatório de estágio curricular enquadra-se no âmbito do Mestrado em Engenharia Informática - Computação Móvel (MEI-CM) da Escola Superior de Tecnologia e Gestão (ESTG) do Instituto Politécnico de Leiria (IPL), tendo sido desenvolvido como parte dos requisitos para a conclusão do respetivo ciclo de estudos. O estágio decorreu durante o ano letivo de 2025/2026, com duração de 9 meses (1400 horas), na empresa Glartek, tendo como principais objetivos a integração no departamento de Quality Assurance (QA) e a contribuição para a validação da qualidade do produto digital desenvolvido pela mesma. Este contexto permitiu adquirir competências práticas na área de testes de software, bem como uma compreensão do ciclo de desenvolvimento no contexto Agile, por meio da aplicação da metodologia Scrum, evidenciando a importância do papel do QA na entrega contínua de software. Ao longo do estágio, foram realizadas diversas atividades integradas no ciclo de testes durante o desenvolvimento de software, incluindo testes manuais, reporte de bugs, desenvolvimento e manutenção de testes automatizados, análise do estado das pipelines de Continuous Integration (CI)/Continuous Delivery (CD) e análise de requisitos, critérios de aceitação e mockups presentes nas user stories. Numa fase inicial, foi efetuado o estudo do produto digital desenvolvido pela empresa (backoffice e aplicação para dispositivos móveis), bem como a adaptação às ferramentas de automação de testes de software, nomeadamente o Cypress para a plataforma web (backoffice), o Patrol para a aplicação móvel em Flutter e o GitLab como ferramenta de gestão de projetos. Posteriormente, procedeu-se à manutenção da bateria de testes automatizados existente, na qual foi possível aplicar boas práticas com vista à redução de flaky tests, contribuindo para uma maior fiabilidade dos resultados e para a otimização do processo de testes. Em suma, o estágio proporcionou a oportunidade de contacto com o mundo do trabalho, permitindo desenvolver competências na área de testes de software, especialmente em dispositivos móveis, bem como compreender as várias atividades necessárias para garantir a qualidade das aplicações, desde o design das funcionalidades, o desenvolvimento e os testes até à sua disponibilização nas lojas de aplicações.

records.title: A Cloud-Based Test Automation Framework for CRM Applications Using Selenium WebDriver: Architecture, Workflow, and Evaluation
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.authors: urvish Gajjar
records.abstract: Customer Relationship Management (CRM) platforms are now delivered almost exclusively as cloud-hosted Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) products that release new functionality several times a year. This release cadence, combined with highly dynamic, asynchronous user interfaces built on technologies such as Shadow DOM and Lightning Web Components, makes manual regression testing slow, expensive, and error-prone. Selenium WebDriver remains the most widely adopted open-source tool for browser-based test automation because it is free, cross-browser, and language-agnostic, yet a plain Selenium script does not, by itself, solve the maintainability, scalability, and reporting problems that CRM cloud applications introduce. This paper proposes a seven-layer, cloud-enabled Selenium WebDriver test automation framework purpose-built for CRM SaaS applications. The framework combines the Page Object Model for maintainability, data-driven execution for coverage, a cloud-hosted Selenium Grid for cross-browser scalability, and Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for repeatable, on-demand regression. We describe the framework's architecture, present a step-by-step execution workflow, discuss implementation details using Java, TestNG, WebDriverManager, and Jenkins, and illustrate the framework with a representative case study on a CRM Leads-Accounts-Opportunities module. The discussion also identifies the residual challenges, such as Shadow DOM penetration and test flakiness, that any CRM automation initiative must still manage. The proposed framework is intended as a practical reference architecture for QA teams and as a foundation for future research on self-healing, AI-assisted CRM test automation.

records.abstract: # Artifact for ICST 2026 Paper <!-- **A Systematic Evaluation of Environmental Flakiness in JavaScript Tests** --> This repository contains the artifact accompanying the ICST 2026 research paper: *A Systematic Evaluation of Environmental Flakiness in JavaScript Tests.* **Authors:** Negar Hashemi, Amjed Tahir, August Shi, Shawn Rasheed, Rachel Blagojevic The artifact includes the dataset, results, and the implementation of the mitigation tool **js-env-sanitizer** used in the study. --- # Badges Requested We are applying for the following badges. ## Available The artifact is publicly available via an archival repository [Zenodo](10.5281/zenodo.18899763) and contains all the data and code necessary to inspect the study. The repository includes: - The dataset used in the empirical study - The summarized experimental results reported in the paper - The implementation of the mitigation tool *js-env-sanitizer* These materials allow researchers to access and reuse the resources produced in this work. ## Reviewed The artifact includes the implementation of **js-env-sanitizer**, a tool that enables developers to annotate tests and test blocks with environment conditions so that tests can be automatically skipped when executed in incompatible environments. The artifact is structured to support reuse by other researchers. The dataset, results, and tool implementation are clearly separated and documented. Researchers can reuse: - the dataset of analyzed projects, - the experimental results for further analysis, and - the **js-env-sanitizer**, a tool for detecting or mitigating environment-dependent flaky tests. We provide a step-by-step instruction on how to execute the artifact. --- # Purpose The goal of this artifact is to support the reproducibility and transparency of the ICST 2026 paper: *A Systematic Evaluation of Environmental Flakiness in JavaScript Tests.* The paper investigates how environmental differences in operating systems, Node.js versions, and browser environments influence the behaviour of JavaScript test suites. The artifact provides three main components: 1. **Dataset** A dataset of JavaScript projects analysed in the empirical study. 2. **Experimental Results** The summarized results from the empirical evaluation of environmental flakiness. 3. **Mitigation Tool** The implementation of **js-env-sanitizer**, a lightweight tool that allows developers to annotate tests with environment conditions and automatically skip incompatible tests. --- # Provenance The artifact can be obtained from the archival repository: **Zenodo DOI:** 10.5281/zenodo.18899763 Paper preprint (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.19098 A copy of the paper is also included in the artifact under: paper/EnvFlakiness_ICST2026.pdf --- # Artifact Structure The artifact comprises three main components. Empirical-evaluation/ dataset/ projectStatistics.csv results/ evaluationResults.csv Mitigation/ js-env-sanitizer/ index.js sanitizer.js setup.js package.json evaluation/ toolEvaluationResults.csv paper/ EnvFlakiness_ICST2026.pdf --- ## Dataset Directory: `Empirical-evaluation/dataset/projectStatistics.csv` This file contains the list of JavaScript projects analyzed in the empirical study together with basic statistics used in the evaluation. The projects were collected from open-source repositories hosted on GitHub. The dataset represents a collection of JavaScript projects used to investigate environment-dependent test behaviour. ## Experimental Results Directory: `Empirical-evaluation/results/evaluationResults.csv` This file contains the summarized results of the empirical analysis of environmental flakiness across the dataset. ## Mitigation Evaluation Results Directory: `Mitigation/evaluation/toolEvaluationResults.csv` This file contains the results of evaluating the mitigation approach implemented in **js-env-sanitizer**. ## Ethical and Legal Considerations The dataset consists of metadata about publicly available open-source projects. No private data or sensitive information is included in the artifact. All analyzed projects originate from publicly accessible repositories and are used only for research purposes. ## Storage Requirements The artifact is lightweight and requires only a small amount of storage space (<100 megabytes). --- # Setup ## Hardware Requirements No special hardware is required to use this artifact. The artifact can be executed on any standard computer capable of running Node.js. ## Software Requirements To execute the tool implementation, the following software is required: - Node.js (version 18 or later recommended) - npm (Node Package Manager) No additional dependencies, such as GPUs or specialized hardware, are required. --- # Installation Navigate to the tool directory: ``cd Mitigation/js-env-sanitizer`` Install dependencies using npm: ``npm install`` --- # Usage ## Basic Usage Example The tool can be initialized using the setup script: ``node setup.js`` This prepares the sanitizer so that test annotations can be interpreted when running test suites. Example of a test annotated with environment conditions: ``` /** * @skipOnOS windows */ test("example test", () => { // test implementation }); ``` When executed in a Windows environment, the test will be skipped automatically. This allows developers to prevent environment-dependent flaky tests from failing in continuous integration environments. --- ## Reproducing Results from the Paper The empirical results reported in the ICST 2026 paper are provided in the artifact. Main empirical results: `Empirical-evaluation/results/evaluationResults.csv` Mitigation evaluation results: `Mitigation/evaluation/toolEvaluationResults.csv` These files correspond to the summarized results discussed in the paper and can be used for further analysis or validation. --- # License This artifact is released under the MIT License. records.title: Detection of HIV ‐1 Antibodies in Saliva of Persons Living With HIV Using Blood‐Based First Response HIV 1‐2.O Card Test
records.venue: Journal of Clinical Laboratory Analysis
records.authors: Enoch Aninagyei; Comfort Addo Boatey; Gifty Larbi; Wilson Bright Tsidi; Raphael Eyram Amemo; Ebenezer Tawiah Nyarkotey; Godknows Afenya; Desmond Omane Acheampong
records.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study tested HIV-1 antibodies in saliva samples (sHIV-1 Ab) collected by the Self-Lollisponge device. METHODS: Blood and saliva from confirmed persons with HIV and HIV-negative controls were analyzed for HIV-1/2 antibodies using the blood-based First Response HIV 1-2.O Card Test. The sampling device containing sHIV-1 Ab was stored at 6°C for 60 days, with intermittent testing on days 2, 5, 10, 20, 30, and 60. Regression analysis was done to assess the relationship between the presence of sHIV-1 Ab and independent variables. RESULTS: The sensitivity and the specificity of detecting sHIV-1 Ab were 72.9% (95% CI: 63.92%-80.65%) and 100% (95% CI: 92.89%-100.00%), respectively. The presence of opportunistic infections (AOR = 13.1, p < 0.001), having stomatorrhagia (AOR = 4.56, p = 0.0022), and hyperviremia (> 201 copies/mL) (AOR = 4.91, p = 0.0225) heightened sHIV-1 Ab detection. Furthermore, fatigue (AOR = 12.1, p = 0.0024), fever (AOR = 3.5, p = 0.0144), and weight loss (AOR = 10.9, p = 0.0318) increased the odds of having sHIV-1 Ab in persons living with HIV (PLWHIV). sHIV-1 Ab was identified in over 90% of PLWHIV with opportunistic infections (OIs) and stomatorrhagia, OIs and hyperviremia, and stomatorrhagia and hyperviremia. Upon storage for 60 days, the sHIV-1 Ab was detected in all the samples. CONCLUSION: Saliva could be an alternative to blood for diagnosing HIV. In addition, the Self-Lollisponge device was found to be user-friendly, acquiescent to all settings, and cheap, and can preserve sHIV-1 Ab for at least 60 days.

records.title: Test Automation in Mobile Platforms: Process Optimisation under Agile Methodologies in an Industrial Context
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.authors: José Ribeiro; Bernardo Melo
records.abstract: Abstract:This study outlines the practical use of mobile verification and validation processes in industrial software development. It explores the main challenges posed by manual and automated testing, continuous integration/continuous deployment, device fragmentation, and flaky end-to-end tests. The research takes place in an Agile (Scrum) context at a software company that develops a platform for frontline workers, combining a mobile app with a web-based back-office and incorporating Artificial Intelligence features. In this context, ensuring the quality of incremental deliveries requires balancing exploratory manual testing with automated end-to-end testing while addressing the instability and challenges commonly associated with mobile UI automation. The main challenge is maintaining the reliability and credibility of the automated test suite, especially in the presence of incomplete acceptance criteria, fast-paced development cycles, and other factors that affect the mobile testing cycle more broadly, such as limited device access and differences between emulators and real devices. Finally, the paper presents practical strategies to mitigate test flakiness and synthesises lessons learned to improve mobile testing practices in industrial contexts, including recommended approaches to test design, isolation, and early involvement in the development lifecycle.Context Note: This document shares lessons learned and best practices regarding mobile application testing in an industrial context.

records.title: AI-assisted automation testing : methodologies, tools, limitations and the role of human oversight
records.venue: Νημερτής
records.authors: Αντωνία Μπάρκα
records.abstract: Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία εξετάζει τον ρόλο της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης στον αυτοματισμό ελέγχου λογισμικού (test automation), με έμφαση στις τεχνικές, στα εργαλεία, στους περιορισμούς και στις προϋποθέσεις υπεύθυνης χρήσης τους. Η σύγχρονη ανάπτυξη λογισμικού χαρακτηρίζεται από συχνές αλλαγές, αυξημένη πολυπλοκότητα, απαιτήσεις για γρήγορα release cycles και ανάγκη συνεχούς διασφάλισης ποιότητας. Παρότι το παραδοσιακό automation testing έχει καθιερωθεί ως βασικό στοιχείο των Agile και DevOps πρακτικών, εξακολουθεί να αντιμετωπίζει προκλήσεις, όπως η ευθραυστότητα (fragility) των UI tests, τα flaky tests, το αυξημένο κόστος συντήρησης και η δυσκολία ανάλυσης αποτυχιών σε μεγάλα CI/CD pipelines. Στο πλαίσιο αυτό, η εργασία αναλύει την έννοια του AI-assisted automation testing ως μια συμπληρωματική και όχι πλήρως αυτόνομη προσέγγιση. Παρουσιάζονται βασικές τεχνικές machine learning, computer vision, search-based software testing, static analysis, symbolic execution και large language models, και εξετάζονται αντιπροσωπευτικά εργαλεία που καλύπτουν διαφορετικά στάδια του testing lifecycle: το Playwright ως ντετερμινιστικό baseline, το Applitools για visual AI testing, το Testim (Tricentis) για self-healing UI automation, το mabl για intelligent execution analytics, και τα EvoSuite και Diffblue Cover για αυτόματη παραγωγή unit tests με ερευνητικό και βιομηχανικό προσανατολισμό αντίστοιχα. Το θεωρητικό και συγκριτικό μέρος συμπληρώνεται από μια ολοκληρωμένη υλοποίηση (case study), η οποία αποτελεί και την κύρια πρωτότυπη συνεισφορά της εργασίας. Αναπτύχθηκε ένα πλαίσιο αξιολόγησης που συγκρίνει τρία επίπεδα ελέγχου, ένα ντετερμινιστικό baseline σε Playwright, έναν μηχανισμό self-healing locators βασισμένο σε σταθμισμένη ομοιότητα χαρακτηριστικών, και ένα επίπεδο visual checkpoints, έναντι ενός καταλόγου ελεγχόμενων μεταλλάξεων (controlled mutations) της διεπαφής. Επιπλέον υλοποιήθηκε ένα βήμα LLM-assisted failure analysis με ρητή ανθρώπινη επιβεβαίωση. Η πειραματική διάταξη είναι πλήρως αναπαραγώγιμη και επιτρέπει την ποσοτική μέτρηση του πού η τεχνητή νοημοσύνη προσθέτει αξία και πού εισάγει κίνδυνο. Η εργασία καταλήγει ότι η αξία της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης στο testing δεν βρίσκεται στην αντικατάσταση του tester, αλλά στην ενίσχυση (augmentation) της ικανότητάς του να διαχειρίζεται πολυπλοκότητα, να μειώνει επαναλαμβανόμενο φόρτο και να λαμβάνει πιο τεκμηριωμένες αποφάσεις. Η ανθρώπινη εποπτεία, η explainability, η αξιοπιστία και η υπεύθυνη ενσωμάτωση των εργαλείων παραμένουν κρίσιμες προϋποθέσεις για την επιτυχή αξιοποίησή τους.

records.title: Predictive Quality Engineering in Distributed Data Platforms Using Machine Learning
records.venue: IEEE International Systems Conference (SysCon)
records.authors: Jay Bharat Mehta
records.abstract: This article examines the role of predictive quality engineering in distributed data platforms by applying machine learning techniques to telemetry data. Modern software systems emit large volumes of logs, metrics, and traces, yet much of this data remains underutilized for quality assurance and failure prevention. This paper presents a practical framework that integrates telemetry ingestion, preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, and real-time feedback loops to enable early detection of reliability risks. The framework is illustrated through three representative use cases: log anomaly detection, prediction of test flakiness in CI pipelines, and forecasting of performance regressions.In operational deployments used as case studies, the approach reduced major incident frequency by approximately 70%, decreased mean time to resolution by more than 65%, and improved detection of unstable test behavior with F1-scores above 0.85 when compared to rule-based baselines. Rather than proposing a novel algorithm, this work focuses on the systems architecture, engineering practices, and deployment considerations required to operationalize predictive quality engineering in real-world environments. The results suggest that telemetry-driven predictive methods can transform quality assurance from a reactive activity into a proactive engineering discipline.

Intermittent trials consisted of 90 s at 40 % VP2 max) a 5 s rest, a maximal sprint of - 6 s (constant work) and a passive rest of - 15-20 s. Continuous trials consisted of cycling at 60 r.p.m. at the same average exercise intensity as that achieved during the intermittent test. At the end of each 30 min trial subjects cycled to exhaustion at 100% Vo2max Thermal, physiological and metabolic variables were recorded at 5 min intervals and at exhaustion throughout all trials. records.title: Data Science for Software Maintenance
records.venue: UWSpace (University of Waterloo)
records.authors: Laura Inozemtseva
records.abstract: Maintaining and evolving modern software systems is a difficult task: their scope and complexity mean that seemingly inconsequential changes can have far-reaching consequences. Most software development companies attempt to reduce the number of faults introduced by adopting maintenance processes. These processes can be developed in various ways. In this thesis, we argue that data science techniques can be used to support process development. Specifically, we claim that robust development processes are necessary to minimize the number of faults introduced when evolving complex software systems. These processes should be based on empirical research findings. Data science techniques allow software engineering researchers to develop research insights that may be difficult or impossible to obtain with other research methodologies. These research insights support the creation of development processes. Thus, data science techniques support the creation of empirically-based development processes. We support this argument with three examples. First, we present insights into automated malicious Android application (app) detection. Many of the prior studies done on this topic used small corpora that may provide insufficient variety to create a robust app classifier. Currently, no empirically established guidelines for corpus size exist, meaning that previous studies have used anywhere from tens of apps to hundreds of thousands of apps to draw their conclusions. This variability makes it difficult to judge if the findings of any one study generalize. We attempted to establish such guidelines and found that 1,000 apps may be sufficient for studies that are concerned with what the majority of apps do, while more than a million apps may be required in studies that want to identify outliers. Moreover, many prior studies of malicious app detection used outdated malware corpora in their experiments that, combined with the rapid evolution of the Android API, may have influenced the accuracy of the studies. We investigated this problem by studying 1.3 million apps and showed that the evolution of the API does affect classifier accuracy, but not in the way we originally predicted. We also used our API usage data to identify the most infrequently used API methods. The use of data science techniques allowed us to study an order of magnitude more apps than previous work in the area; additionally, our insights into infrequently used methods illustrate how data science can be used to guide API deprecation. Second, we present insights into the costs and benefits of regression testing. Regression test suites grow over time, and while a comprehensive suite can detect faults that are introduced into the system, such a suite can be expensive to write, maintain, and execute. These costs may or may not be justified, depending on the number and severity of faults the suite can detect. By studying 61 projects that use Travis CI, a continuous integration system, we were able to characterize the cost/benefit tradeoff of their test suites. For example, we found that only 74% of non-flaky test failures are caused by defects in the system under test; the other 26% were caused by incorrect or obsolete tests and thus represent a maintenance cost rather than a benefit of the suite. Data about the costs and benefits of testing can help system maintainers understand whether their test suite is a good investment, shaping their subsequent maintenance decisions. The use of data science techniques allowed us to study a large number of projects, increasing the external generalizability of the study and making the insights gained more useful. Third, we present insights into the use of mutants to replace real faulty programs in testing research. Mutants are programs that contain deliberately injected faults, where the faults are generated by applying mutation operators. Applying an operator means making a small change to the program source code, such as replacing a constant with another constant. The use of mutants is appealing because large numbers of mutants can be automatically generated and used when known faults are unavailable or insufficient in number. However, prior to this work, there was little experimental evidence to support the use of mutants as a replacement for real faults. We studied this problem and found that, in general, mutants are an adequate substitute for faults when conducting testing research. That is, a test suite’s ability to detect mutants is correlated with its ability to detect real faults that developers have fixed, for both developer-written and automatically-generated test suites. However, we also found that additional mutation operators should be developed and some classes of faults cannot be generated via mutation. The use of data science techniques was an essential part of generating the set of real faults used in the study. Taken together, the results of these three studies provide evidence that data science techniques allow software engineering researchers to develop insights that are difficult or impossible to obtain using other research methodologies

records.title: Differences In Performance Traits In Intermittent Versus Continuous Exercise Testing Of Handball Players and Triathletes
records.venue: Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise
records.authors: Björn Sterzing; Tobias Ehlert; Sarah A. Breitbach; Perikles D. Simon
records.abstract: External validity of endurance performance diagnostics may depend on type of sports. In order to reflect different load quality for the muscle specific endurance testing regimes have been developed for intermittent sports. Here we examined the influence of an intermittent versus a typical continuous step-wise progressive treadmill protocol on metabolic and cardiorespiratory parameters. PURPOSE: To determine if handball players (HB) in comparison to triathletes (T) show differences in typical submaximal lactate thresholds (LT and LT + 1.5 mmol), or in VO2max depending on either continuous or intermittent type of a step-wise progressive exercise testing. METHODS: 13 HB and 13 T; mean (SD) age 24.7 (3.1 yrs) height 184.2 (7.2 cm), weight 82.7 (10.8 kg) with a training load of 6.8 (3.1) h/wk in HB versus 8.8 (3.3) h/wk in T. Each subject performed two treadmill protocols within one week. First a typical step-wise incremental treadmill test (CTT) starting at 6 km/h increasing every 3 min by 2 km/h until exhaustion. Second a step-wise incremental intermittent test (IMT) with steps split into 6x15s load phase interlaced with 6x15s active recovery. Load phase started at 8km/h and was increased every 3 min by 2 km/h, while active recovery remained at 6 km/h throughout all steps until exhaustion. VO2max, velocity at LT, velocity at LT + 1.5 mmol/l lactate (IAT). RESULTS: VO2max in ml/min/kg was not significantly different between sports and testing protocols (all 4 groups) with CTT for HB 50.5 (4.7) and T 53.2 (3.5), or with IMT 50.1 (3.7) in HB and 51.2 (4.2) for T. Velocity in km/h at IAT was not significantly different between all groups with CTT for HB 11.9 (0.8) and 12.4 (1.3) for T, or with IMT 11.2 (0.4) for HB and 11.5 (0.7) for T. For the LT in km/h we revealed in an analysis of co-variance a slightly significantly higher velocity of ΔV = 0,74 km/h (95% CI = 0,03-1,45, p < 0.04) in T than in HB in CTT. CONCLUSIONS: We recruited a collective of HB and T with an almost comparable weekly training load. HB and T showed comparable typical performance trait characteristics for the higher work-load demand (VO2max and IAT), which was even independent of type of test. The slightly better performance of T in specifically the continuous test setting principally reflects higher load and potentially a better adaptation to this type of working demand.

records.title: Automated Infrastructure-as-Code Testing at Enterprise Scale: A Longitudinal Study of Terratest Adoption Across Heterogeneous Repository Architectures
records.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
records.authors: Satya Sampreeth Boppudi; Dedeepya Yarra; Saketh Gowerneni; Pradeep Kandepaneni
records.abstract: Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) testing remains an underinvestigated practice in enterprise DevOps, despite IaC defects causing production outages of equivalent severity to application code defects. This paper presents a 12-month longitudinal study of Terratest adoption at a large-scale US energy company, spanning five heterogeneous repository architecture types: pure Terraform networking, mixed Terraform/Ansible compute, ECS-heavy container infrastructure, Lambdaheavy serverless, and multi-cloud hybrid deployments. We document the full adoption trajectory from 0% to 55.2% blended infrastructure test coverage, characterize a defect taxonomy across 300+ detected defects classified into four categories (networking configuration, compute provisioning, storage policy, and application infrastructure), and quantify regression prevention outcomes including 15+ prevented production regressions and rollback frequency reduction from 6 per quarter to near zero. Parallel ECS test runners introduced at month 6 reduced suite execution time from 45 minutes to 12 minutes - a 4x improvement - resolving the primary CI/CD pipeline integration barrier. Cost-benefit analysis yields estimated annual savings of $180K against a $20K total program cost, producing a first-year return on investment exceeding 800%. Three structural barriers to enterprise IaC testing adoption are identified and analyzed: Go language unfamiliarity among infrastructure teams, test flakiness induced by cloud API non-determinism, and long test execution times under sequential execution. These findings provide the first multi-architecture longitudinal dataset for IaC testing adoption at production scale and a practitioner reference for organizations initiating Terratest programs.

records.title: Exploring the Effectiveness of End-to-End Testing Frameworks in Modern Web Development
records.venue: International Journal of Emerging Research in Engineering and Technology
records.authors: Swetha Talakola
records.abstract: Dependability and quality of software constitute first issues in contemporary web development. Traditional testing approaches cannot find integration problems among multiple components as web systems get ever more complicated. Since end-to- end (E2E) testing tools help developers replicate real-world user interactions and validate the complete running performance of an application, they are becoming more and more crucial. The need of E2E testing in improving software dependability is investigated in this work. It underlines the main benefits of early defect discovery, enhanced user experience assurance, and thorough E2E testing system coverage of improvements. Furthermore included are issues that could undermine the effectiveness of automated testing systems: test flakiness, high maintenance overhead, and extended running times. Examining important E2E testing systems including Cypress, Selenium, and Playwright, this paper offers a thorough assessment based on their strengths, weaknesses, and fit for various project objectives. Modern DevOps systems first concentrate on analyzing important components including simplicity of use, performance, debugging tools, and interface. Furthermore, best practices for executing E2E testing include CI/CD pipeline integration, test case design optimization, and artificial intelligence-powered automation applied to raise test dependability. A real case study using an E2E testing infrastructure shows how a large financial company improved test stability and deployment efficiency. This study investigates emerging E2E testing trends including low-code/no-code testing solutions, cloud-based testing, and artificial intelligence-driven automation and so influences the course of software quality assurance. The results emphasize the need of applying scalable, efficient, sustainable E2E testing techniques to guarantee strong and remarkable online applications in a development environment running ever quicker.

ESM-2/ESMFold

ESM-2 and ESMFold are new state-of-the-art Transformer protein language and folding models from Meta AI's Fundamental AI Research Team (FAIR). ESM-2 is trained with a masked language modeling objective, and it can be easily transferred to sequence and token classification tasks for proteins. Checkpoints exist in various sizes, from 8 million parameters up to a huge 15 billion parameter model.

ESMFold is a state-of-the-art single sequence protein folding model which produces high accuracy predictions significantly faster. Unlike previous protein folding tools like AlphaFold2 and openfold, ESMFold uses a pretrained protein language model to generate token embeddings that are used as input to the folding model, and so does not require a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) of related proteins as input. As a result, proteins can be folded in a single forward pass of the model without requiring any external databases or search/alignment tools to be present at inference time. This hugely reduces the time and compute requirements for folding.

Transformer protein language models were introduced in the paper Biological structure and function emerge from scaling unsupervised learning to 250 million protein sequences by Alexander Rives, Joshua Meier, Tom Sercu, Siddharth Goyal, Zeming Lin, Jason Liu, Demi Guo, Myle Ott, C. records.abstract: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/23197219. ## Summary The authors (Meta) present REAP, an automated pipeline that curates execution-based coding-agent benchmarks from real developer-agent sessions, without manual labeling. The motivation is one I live daily: public benchmarks diverge from production workloads in language distribution, prompt style, codebase structure, task mix, and contamination risk, while online A/B testing is slow and shadow deployment is not reproducible. REAP applies three verification filters — LLM-based task classification, agentic test-relevance validation, and multi-run stability checks — to turn noisy production sessions into trustworthy fail-to-pass tasks. Using REAP they curate Harvest, a benchmark of verbatim developer prompts paired with executable tests, spanning 4+ languages with a Hack majority (a real divergence from Python-skewed public benchmarks). Five frontier models score 42.9% to 58.2%, surfacing capability differences the authors say informed concrete deployment decisions. The paper is refreshingly specific about monorepo constraints: ephemeral build infrastructure, expiring toolchains and indices, and the "time travel" problem that makes rolling re-curation a prerequisite rather than a convenience. Accepted at the ASE 2026 Industry Showcase. The source corpus cannot be released; the authors share methodology, classifier prompts, and annotation protocols instead. ## Strengths 1. Solves the right problem. Verbatim prompts, one-to-one prompt-to-diff mapping via AI-provenance instrumentation, and execution-based scoring with no LLM judges — this is how you build an eval that production teams can actually gate deployments on. The explicit rejection of LLM-judge scoring deserves emphasis. 2. Rolling re-curation is the honest answer to benchmark staleness. The paper's argument that manual verification cannot be sustained at monorepo cadence, so automation is a prerequisite, is well made and matches industrial reality. 3. The test-relevance filter is a real contribution. Naively running CI per candidate is computationally infeasible in a monorepo; selecting a small set of causally-connected, stable fail-to-pass tests is the load-bearing engineering of this work, and the near-human classifier accuracy validation is a solid check. 4. Clear-eyed about the contamination problem. Frozen benchmarks leak into training data; a continuously re-curated benchmark that post-dates model cutoffs is one of the few structural fixes available. ## Major comments 1. The corpus cannot be released, so the headline results are unverifiable. The authors share methodology and prompts but not Harvest itself. I understand the proprietary constraint, but it means the 42.9–58.2% solve rates and the deployment decisions they "informed" rest entirely on trust. At minimum, the paper should release a fully worked synthetic or open-source analogue so the pipeline's output quality can be independently inspected. 2. Scope is narrow for the generality of the claims. The case study is one production assistant, single-turn conversations only, and a Hack-majority task pool. Multi-turn sessions — where agents actually fail in production — are excluded by a "deliberate scope choice." The paper should either demonstrate a multi-turn slice or clearly fence the claims. 3. Agent-run stability is not measured. The pipeline checks test flakiness across runs, but agents are non-deterministic: pass@1 from a single run per model is a point estimate with unknown variance. A benchmark meant for deployment gating needs per-task run-to-run variance of the agent itself, not just of the tests. 4. The agentic test-relevance validator is itself an LLM judgment. The paper validates classifiers against human judgment, which is good — but the "causal connection" between test and diff is the most subtle judgment in the pipeline, and false positives here silently corrupt the benchmark's signal. Report the validator's precision/recall on a human-adjudicated sample explicitly. ## Minor comments 1. The paper's title changed across versions (ProdCodeBench to REAP); the final framing as a pipeline paper is the right one — Harvest is an instance, not the contribution. 2. A cost accounting of the curation pipeline itself (compute per admitted task) would help other organizations budget for adoption. ## Overall assessment Recommend with revisions. The methodology is strong and the industrial grounding is real — this is one of the few benchmark papers written by people who have felt the pain of evals that don't transfer. But a non-releasable corpus plus single-run agent scores means the deployment-relevant claims need tighter fencing before this can serve as a template others trust.
